claims.claim: The harness inputs are frozen upstream and PR revisions with per-file SHA-256 hashes.

Both frozen Lua algorithms silently under-enforce under mixed writer configurations on Redis 8.10.2 and Red Hat Valkey 8.0.11: sliding history is deleted early and a depleted token bucket regains full capacity early after shortened expiry.
EVAL and EVALSHA have equal normalized lifecycle semantics and equal invariant outcomes in the executed gate.
The frozen plain-command revision contains source-proven settlement, concurrency, cap, and TTL blockers.
Frozen layouts reject atomically or are decomposed by redis-rs; dynamic cleanup can access a key owned by another primary.
Exact shared aggregate semantics and cross-primary subject distribution are mutually incompatible without a contract change or coordination layer.
The terms-gated Red Hat Valkey repository is served from authenticated registry.redhat.io rather than registry.access.redhat.com; the exact requested manifest digest was preserved and executed.
Pre-execution source and requirements claims remain traced in the local audited proposal.
The mixed-configuration repair passes the same standalone semantic and mismatch-before-mutation suite on both exact products under EVAL and EVALSHA.

The repair passes cached-primary, unavailable-Sentinel, replication-health, ambiguous-timeout, planned failover, unplanned shutdown, cold-script, and post-failover enforcement scenarios on both products.
Cached Sentinel steady state has command/round-trip parity with standalone. No numeric latency or throughput claim is made from the local functional host.
